text: . Delhi Government has approved the DURGA scheme aimed at providing safe, clean and dignified employment opportunities to women and transgender persons in the capital. This decision was taken at a cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Rekha Gupta in New Delhi today. Under this scheme, 1,300 pink electric autos will be allocated in the first phase, 1,170 will be reserved for women and 130 for transgender beneficiaries.The Chief Minister said the scheme will give women and transgender persons an opportunity to become owners and drivers of electric autos. She said that a maximum of 90 electric autos for women and up to 10 electric autos for transgender beneficiaries will be allocated in each revenue district. Ms Gupta said the scheme is an initiative towards making Delhi a safer, greener and more inclusive city.

. Eleven more children have died with suspected measles symptoms in Bangladesh in the past 24 hours, taking the total number of deaths from confirmed measles and suspected cases to 1,076 since March 15, according to the Directorate General of Health Services. The DGHS said 1,157 new suspected measles cases were reported in the past 24 hours, taking the total number of suspected cases to 183,449 since March 15.The number of confirmed measles cases increased by 113 to 20,851 during the same period. Since March 15, a total of 162,048 suspected measles patients have been admitted to hospitals, while 155,612 patients have recovered and been discharged. The DGHS said all 11 deaths reported in the past 24 hours were among suspected measles cases. No death from confirmed measles was reported during the period. Since March 15, 975 children have died from suspected measles, while 101 deaths have been confirmed as measles-related.

. Russia has launched a fresh wave of drone attacks on Kyiv and other parts of Ukraine today, killing at least two people and injuring 23. The attacks came as Zelenskyy began a visit to the United States to address world leaders at the United Nations General Assembly.According to Ukrainian officials in the southeastern city of Zaporizhzhia, two men were injured after a Russian strike hit a shopping mall, triggering a large fire. The latest Russian attacks followed a series of Ukrainian strikes on targets inside Russia, including oil refineries that are considered important to the country’s energy sector and economy.Meanwhile, Russia’s Defence Ministry said its forces had carried out strikes against Ukrainian military-industrial and energy facilities, logistics centres and sea vessels. The latest exchange of attacks underscores the continuing intensity of long-range strikes between Russia and Ukraine, even as diplomatic efforts to explore possible steps towards reducing the fighting remain on the international agenda.

. Vultures are extremely important for our ecosystem. By feeding on dead animals, they help keep the environment clean and reduce the spread of harmful diseases.However, vulture populations have declined significantly because of habitat loss, poisoning, and certain veterinary medicines that are harmful to them. Conservation efforts are therefore essential to protect these birds and maintain the balance of nature.On this International Vulture Day, government and environmental experts have urged people to understand, protect, and conserve vultures for a healthier environment.

. Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) in association with the Border Security Force has seized 12 Kg of gold smuggled from Bangladesh.The Ministry of Finance said that there have been a number of crackdowns across India-Bangladesh border to tap the cross-border gold smuggling. It noted that around 12 KGs of foreign-origin gold worth 17 crore rupees has been seized from different locations of Bihar and Bengal sharing border with Bangladesh. The recovery showcases the vulnerability of the region for such smuggling.The Ministry of Finance said that during 20th to 21st of the month, BSF personnel recovered 27 pieces of unclaimed foreign origin smuggled gold weighing around 3.15 kg near India Bangladesh Border Road and DRI took up the proceedings and seized the gold under the provisions of the Customs Act, 1962.In yet another recovery, in West Bengal, BSF personnel recovered 10 pieces of foreign origin smuggled gold weighing around 1.16 kg in Village Hathkhola, ahead of India Bangladesh Border Fence.

. President Droupadi Murmu has congratulated Roshibina Devi Naorem on winning the Silver Medal in the Women’s 60kg Sanda event in wushu at the Asian Games 2026. In a social media post, the president said winning three medals at three consecutive Asian Games is a remarkable achievement and historic milestone for Indian Wushu. Murmu added that their inspiring journey continues with many more proud moments.She also congratulated Satnam Singh and Salman Khan on winning the Bronze Medal in the Men’s Double Sculls at the Asian Games 2026. She said that their performance reflects the strength of teamwork, endurance and commitment that rowing demands. Murmu added that both continue to achieve greater heights.President Droupadi Murmu has congratulated the Indian Men’s Badminton Team on winning Bronze Medal at the Asian Games 2026. In a social media post, the President said, this commendable achievement reflects the team’s determination, resilience and fighting spirit. President Murmu added that each member made a valuable contribution to this proud success.Prime Minister Narendra Modi also congratulated Naorem Roshibina Devi on winning the Silver Medal in the Women’s Sanda 60kg event at the Asian Games. In a social media post, Mr Modi said that winning medals at three consecutive Asian Games is a remarkable achievement. He said that Naorem Roshibina’s consistency, courage and determination are truly commendable.Mr Modi congratulated Satnam Singh and Salman Khan on winning the bronze medal in the Men’s Double Sculls at the Asian Games. In a social media post, he said that the performance by both athletes has earned India a well-deserved medal. Prime Minister Modi said that their composure and coordination stood out. He stated that this accomplishment will serve as motivation for them to attain even greater heights in the year ahead.

. External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar co-chaired the L.69 Consultative Ministerial Interaction on UNSC reform, along with his Saint Lucian counterpart Alva Baptist. Addressing the meeting, Dr Jaishankar noted that the Global South is at the receiving end of the unprecedented changes that the world is undergoing, with the UN falling short of expectations.He also underlined that the inability of the UN Security Council to address ongoing conflicts and threats to international peace and security only highlights the urgency of reform. He stressed that continuing to delay reform perpetuates historical injustice. He said that the members of the L.69 and C.10 join forces to keep pushing for UNSC reform.The L.69 Group of Developing Countries is a cross-regional coalition of developing nations focused on achieving comprehensive and urgent reform of the United Nations Security Council. The C-10 (Committee of Ten) is an African Union coalition of ten African countries created to champion the Common African Position on the United Nations Security Council.

. The Reserve Bank of India has extended an existing KYC facility available to Non-Resident Indians and Persons of Indian Origin to Foreign Portfolio Investors, allowing banks to accept original certified copies of KYC documents certified by specified authorities abroad.Under the amended directions, banks may accept an original certified copy of Aadhaar-related proof or an officially valid document for FPIs, with the certification done by specified authorities. The certified copies may be attested by authorised officials of overseas branches of Scheduled Commercial Banks registered in India, branches of overseas banks having relationships with Indian banks, Notary Public abroad, Court Magistrate, Judge, or the Indian Embassy/Consulate General in the country where the non-resident customer resides.The amendment was issued on Friday through the RBI (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Amendment Directions, 2026 and came into effect immediately.

. Reigning World Champion D Gukesh and R Praggnanandhaa registered victories as India defeated England 2.5-1.5 in Round 7 of FIDE Chess Olympiad in Samarkand yesterday.Gukesh and Praggnanandhaa secured wins for India, while Arjun Erigaisi was held to a draw by veteran Michael Adams. Nihal Sarin suffered a defeat against Luke McShane. Playing with the white pieces, Praggnanandhaa defeated Nikita Vitiugov, while Gukesh, playing black, defeated Daniel Howard Fernandez. The victory helped defending champions India recover after their defeat to hosts Uzbekistan and keep their campaign on track.In the women’s section, B Savitha Shri continued her remarkable run with a seventh consecutive victory as India defeated Germany 3.5-0.5 in Round 7. Savitha Shri remains the only player at the Olympiad to have won all seven of her games. Koneru Humpy defeated Dinara Wagner, while Divya Deshmukh beat Hanna Marie Klek. Savitha Shri, playing with the black pieces, defeated Lara Schulze. The victory kept India in medal contention with two rounds remaining in the competition.

The Ministry of Education, in coordination with the External Affairs Ministry is organizing a two day Bharat Innovates Exposition from today at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi to showcase India’s Deep-Tech innovations as a lead up to and alongside the 18th BRICS Summit 2026. The Exposition is showcasing 37 India’s Deep-Tech startups and ventures alligning with the theme of India’s BRICS Chairship Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. The event is providing participating innovators an opportunity to network with CEOs, investors, business leaders and industry representatives from BRICS member countries. Ministry of Eduaction said that the event will facilitate opportunities for Business to Business engagements, technology partnerships, investment discussions, business linkages and international market access.

. Election Commission has said that written notes and internal checks are standard, ongoing practice, meant to ensure transparency and legal compliance and these are not signs of dysfunction. In a statement Election Commission said, all official orders and decisions carry full legal sanction under the 2023 Act governing the Commission’s conduct of business. It said, every officer of the Commission, not just the three Commissioners, is authorised to give suggestions for improving the electoral system. The Poll Body said, it has introduced around 40 new initiatives in the past year, all outcomes of unanimous decisions of the full Commission. In this same period, the Commission successfully conducted elections in Bihar, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Assam and West Bengal.

. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said its special US dollar-Indian rupee (USD-INR) forex swap facility has received forex inflows of over 143.5 billion US dollars till September 18, 2026. According to the latest data, Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) [FCNR-B] deposits accounted for the overwhelming majority, amounting to 132.98 billion US dollars. Meanwhile, Overseas Foreign Currency Borrowings (OFCBs) brought in 5.32 billion US dollars and External Commercial Borrowings (ECBs) contributed 5.29 billion US dollars. The Apex Bank introduced the special USD-INR forex swap facility covering FCNR(B) deposits, ECBs and OFCBs inflows on June 8, 2026, to boost the inflow of dollars amid a weakening rupee. The FCNR(B) deposits scheme was closed on August 31, 2026, while the facility for ECBs and OFCBs remains available until December 31, 2026

The Indian Women’s Cricket team reasserted its continental dominance by clinching a second successive gold medal at the Asian Games, thrashing Sri Lanka by 147 runs in the final at Nisshin in Japan today. Opting to bat, India posted 216 for the loss of three wickets in the stipulated 20 overs, the highest total in Asian Games history, riding on Smriti Mandhana’s 79 runs off 45 balls and Richa Ghosh’s 48 off 22. In reply, Sri Lanka were bowled out for just 69 in 15.4 overs. This is India’s first gold medal at the ongoing Asiad and overall seventh medal.Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated the Women’s Cricket Team on the feat. Calling it a splendid triumph for Indian cricket, Mr Modi said that this victory also brings India its first Gold of this edition of the Games. In a social media post, he said that it was a commanding performance marked by confidence, skill, and wonderful teamwork. The Prime Minister said that the team has made the nation proud and will inspire countless young cricketers across the country.Indian men’s Badminton team defeated hosts Japan in the quarterfinals and assured itself of a medal at the Asian Games. Lakshya Sen was staring at defeat after losing the opening game and trailing 14-19 in the decider. However, Lakshya made a comeback, reeling off seven straight points to beat world No.7 and two-time world championships silver-medallist Kodai Naraoka 11-21, 21-5, 21-19 to give India a 1-0 lead. Playing the first doubles, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, who have won two titles this season, registered a 21-18, 24-22 win over former world champions Hoki Takuro and Kobayashi Yugo to extend India’s lead to 2-0. Ayush Shetty then produced an impressive performance to see off world no. 16 Koki Watanabe 21-10 21-19 to seal the match and a medal for India.  The Indian men were the silver-medallists of the last edition.In Wushu, India’s Roshibina Devi also confirmed a medal at the Asian Games after securing a 5-0 win over Chu Man Sin of Macao, in the Women’s 60kg quarterfinals. Roshibina, the 2018 and 2022 Asiad medallist, has now secured a third continental medal with another strong performance to advance to the semifinals. Roshibina will now be in action in the semifinals tomorrow for a place in the final. She is already a silver medallist from the 2023 Asian Games, when she came second in theSanda60 kg category. She also bagged a bronze medal in the 2018 Jakarta Games in the same weight category.Apart from her, India’s Aryan also moved to the quarterfinals as he fights for a medal. Aryan defeated Afghanistan’s Safi Shahzada in the Men’s 56kg pre-quarters 2-0 to progress into the quarterfinals.Indian boxer Jadumani Singh defeated Nepal’s Chandra Bahadur Thapa to march into the pre-quarters in the Men’s 55kg preliminary round at the Nishio Gymnasium in Japan today. Commonwealth Games silver medallist Jadumani registered a unanimous 5-0 win over the reigning World Championships’ bronze medallist Thapa with a brilliant bout. Jadumani will now be up against Filipino boxer Carlo Paalam in the pre-quarters on Saturday. Paalam is a silver medallist from the 2020 Tokyo Olympic Games.Earlier, Glasgow Games gold medallist Sakshi Chaudhary defeated Paris Olympics bronze medallist Aira Villegas in the preliminary round at the Asian Games 2026 to march into the pre-quarters. Sakshi outclassed the Filipino pugilist by a unanimous decision of 5-0. She will be facing current 51kg world champion Alua Balkibekova on Thursday.In Men’s Cricket, India narrowly avoided a historic upset, defeating hosts Japan by two runs in a rain-curtailed, five-overs-a-side one-off T20 International match at the Sano International Cricket Ground today. This was India’s 200th victory in T20 Internationals, including Super Over wins. After a nearly 2.5-hour delay due to a wet outfield, India skipper Shreyas Iyer won the toss and opted to bat first. However, Japan’s spinners made the most of the conditions, restricting the visitors to 32 for 4 after five overs. Chasing 33 off 30 balls, Japan gave India a major scare and came agonisingly close to pulling off one of the biggest upsets in their cricketing history. Washington Sundar struck twice to halt Japan’s momentum, while Axar Patel kept things tight with his experience and control. The hosts managed to score 30 for 3 in five overs and eventually fell two runs short, handing India a nervy victory.

. Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare Anupriya Patel today said that India’s journey in Pharmacovigilance has been a remarkable example of self-reliance over the years. She said this while releasing the 7th Edition of the National Formulary of India in New Delhi. The Minister said that currently more than one thousand one hundred Adverse Drug Reaction Monitoring Centres are operational in the country and the Government aims to increase this number up to the primary health facility level.She also said that 25 countries in the world recognise and accept the Indian pharmacopoeia and added that the country now provides pharmacovigilance data to the WHO patient safety database. The Minister highlighted that India has risen from the 123rd rank in 2014 to the 8th rank in providing this data to WHO. India achieved this milestone in the year 2025. On the occasion, the Minister appealed to the citizens to avoid any form of self-medication, follow professional prescriptions, and never ignore a sudden or unexpected side effect of any medicinal drug.

. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, UAE Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan and French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot participated in the India-UAE-France trilateral on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York. They discussed collaboration in Artificial Intelligence (AI), space, health sciences, energy and culture.The three ministers reviewed progress in trilateral cooperation across agreed areas of mutual interest, including space, energy, artificial intelligence, and culture and heritage.According to the statement released by the Ministry of External Affairs, the leaders also discussed the situation in West Asia.The three ministers emphasised further strengthening and expanding trilateral cooperation in the areas of mutual interest and further building upon the strong and friendly ties that exist between India, France and the UAE.

Finance Ministry has informed that all Public Sector Banks and Regional Rural Banks will remain open on Sunday, 27th of this month for convenience of customers.The Ministry said that this step has been taken in view of the proposed three-day nationwide bank strike called by the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) from 28th to 30th of this month, coinciding with the preceding weekend holidays of 26th and 27th September. It said that the Reserve Bank of India has granted approval for all bank branches, offices, ATM-link branches and Currency Chests to remain fully operational on Sunday. The Ministry said that the Government and bank managements have appealed to unions to defer the proposed strike, and have also taken measures to ensure that essential banking services continue un-interrupted.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has congratulated Soft Tennis player Jay Meena on winning Bronze in the Men’s Individual event and becoming India’s first-ever Asian Games medallist in Soft Tennis. In a social media post, Mr Modi stated that his achievement marked a memorable new chapter for the sport in the Country. The Prime Minister said that this medal will inspire many more youngsters to take up Soft Tennis and excel.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Bihar, East Madhya Pradesh, East Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and North Eastern parts of the country during the next two days. IMD said that thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are likely to prevail over Andhra Pradesh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Bihar, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. Meanwhile, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Mahe are expected to experience hot and humid weather till 8th of this month.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices rebounded today. The Sensex rose 299 points or 0.4 per cent to close at 74,828. The Nifty jumped 118 points or half a per cent to settle at 23,447.In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index climbed 0.7 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index gained 0.9 per cent.

. The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) hasissued redalert for extremely heavy rainfall over isolated places of Chhattisgarh, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Telangana for the next two days. The Met Department has predicted heavy rainfall over Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Bihar, Jharkhand, Kerala, Maharashtra, West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. The weather department also forecast thunderstorms accompanied with highly gusty winds over Madhya Pradesh and Parts of North-East tomorrow.For Delhi, IMD said the national capital will witness mostly clear skies with no rain. The maximum temperature in Delhi is expected to be around 34 to 35 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature of 23 to 25 degrees Celsius.

The second edition of the India Art, Architecture and Design Biennale (IAADB) will be held from 4th December 2026 to 21st March 2027 in New Delhi.The theme of this 108-day Biennale is ‘Tat Tvam Asi – Reconnecting in an Age of Distraction’. Talking exclusively to Akashvani News, Secretary of the Ministry of Culture, Vivek Aggarwal said that, the Biennale will feature art installations at iconic heritage sites of the National Capital, including Purana Qila, Red Fort, Safdarjung Tomb, Qutub Minar, Qila Rai Pithora and Lodhi Garden. He said that the theme of this year’s Biennale directly takes inspiration from India’s ancient traditions and spiritual thought, which emphasize self-introspection and the unity of the individual with the larger universal consciousness.Mr Aggarwal said that the Ministry aims to take IAADB to a global level by encouraging participation from international pavilions and artists, Indian states and the private sector.Speaking about the cultural diplomacy of India, He said that cultural exchange is an important component of cultural diplomacy and the country’s soft power. Mr Aggarwal added that participation of foreign countries will provide an opportunity for Indian and international audiences to experience diverse art forms and will help position the Biennale on the global cultural calendar.Underlining the importance of Art and Design students in this Biennale, He said that the Ministry plans to involve students, particularly those pursuing art and design, in various activities associated with the Biennale, providing them opportunities to engage with artists and the wider creative ecosystem.The second edition of the India Art, Architecture & Design Biennale 2026 is the largest platform which offers artists, curators, galleries, corporates, architects, designers, cultural institutions and other stakeholders a chance to connect with culture and the creative world. This edition is conceived not as a single exhibition in a single location but as a city-wide cultural platform. Visitors will have an opportunity to experience the historical monuments along with contemporary art installations.

. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) today absorbed 71,971 crore rupees from the banking system through an overnight Variable Rate Reverse Repo (VRRR) auction. The operation was conducted to absorb surplus liquidity from the system and align overnight money market rates with the benchmark policy repo rate.According to an official release, the central bank fully accepted all bids received against a total notified auction size of 75,000 crore rupees. The bids were accepted at a cut-off and weighted average rate of 5.24 per cent.As per the RBI data, currently, surplus liquidity in the banking system is estimated to be around 4.92 lakh crore rupees. To manage these conditions, the central bank also conducted two open market operations (OMO), resulting in sales of Government securities worth 50,000 crore rupees on 17th September and 25,000 crore rupees on 21st September. The final tranche of 25,000 crore rupees is scheduled for the 28th of this month.The banking system has been flushed with liquidity primarily due to the heavy mobilization of Foreign Currency Non-Resident deposits, subsequent currency swaps with the central bank, and month-end government expenditure on salaries and pensions.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended 0.4 per cent lower today. The Sensex lost 330 points to close at 74,529. The Nifty dropped 85 points to settle at 23,329.In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Nifty Midcap 100 index dipped 0.1 per cent, while the Nifty Smallcap 100 index declined 0.2 per cent.In the forex market, the rupee depreciated by 22 paise to trade at 95 rupees and 59 paise against the US dollar.In the global crude oil market, Brent Crude was trading 2.6 per cent down at 97 US dollars and 71 cents per barrel, while WTI Crude was trading 3.1 per cent lower at 92 US dollars and 78 cents per barrel in intra-day trade.At the Multi Commodity Exchange, Gold for the October contract was trading 0.4 per cent down at 1,52,511 rupees per 10 grams, and Silver for the December contract was trading half a per cent lower at 2,38,130 rupees per kilogram, when reports last came in.For more updates about the market activities, tune in to Akashvani’s bilingual programme ‘Market Mantra’ at 6:30 PM this evening.

. The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has approved a 200 million dollar loan to help Bangladesh modernize and strengthen its power distribution network in peri-urban areas surrounding Dhaka. Under the Power Distribution Network Enhancement Project, the Bangladesh Rural Electrification Board will upgrade electricity infrastructure across 13 Palli Bidyut Samities, serving rapidly growing industrial and urban areas.The project will install 1,150 megavolt-amperes of new transformer capacity across 52 substations and upgrade 12 existing substations. It will also construct or upgrade more than 2,600 kilometres of distribution lines and introduce technologies for faster fault detection and service restoration.ADB said the project will help address overloaded substations, aging infrastructure, power losses and increasing natural hazard risks, while improving the reliability and efficiency of electricity supply.The project also includes measures to strengthen the institutional capacity and financial sustainability of the power cooperatives.

. Indian men’s Badminton team produced a superlative performance to outwit hosts Japan in the quarterfinals and assure itself of a medal at the Asian Games at Nagoya, Japan, today. Lakshya Sen was staring at defeat after losing the opening game and trailing 14-19 in the decider. However, Lakshya made a comeback, reeling off seven straight points to beat world No.7 and two-time world championships silver-medallist Kodai Naraoka 11-21, 21-5, 21-19 to give India a 1-0 lead. Playing the first doubles, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, who have won two titles this season, registered a 21-18, 24-22 win over former world champions Hoki Takuro and Kobayashi Yugo to extend India’s lead to 2-0. Ayush Shetty then produced an impressive performance to see off world no. 16 Koki Watanabe 21-10, 21-19 to seal the match and a medal for India.India will face the winner of the other quarterfinal between defending champions China and Korea in the last four stage tomorrow. . Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh today held a discussion with the European Parliament delegation focusing on effective implementation of India-EU FTA. The delegation,comprisingmembers of the European Parliament’s Committee on Industry, Research and Energy, met Dr Singh in New Delhi. During the meeting, both sides discussed deepening cooperation in Science, Technology and Emerging Technologies.On the occasion, Dr Singh said the India-EU strategic partnership offers significant opportunities for closer collaboration in areas of mutual priority, with science and research forming an integral part of the partnership. He added that the FTA will open new opportunities for businesses, consumers and skilled professionals and provide further momentum to the multifaceted India-EU strategic partnership.Member of European Parliament Angelika Winzig said that India is a key strategic partner for the European Union. She said the delegation’s visit was aimed at gaining a deeper understanding of India’s industrial and technology policies and identifying areas for closer cooperation.

. Indian wushu player Roshibina Devi Naorem signed off with a Silver medal in the Women’s 60kg Sanda event at the Asian Games after losing 0-2 to China’s Zhang Xiaoyu in the final at Nagoya in Japan. It is third Asian Games medal for Roshibina, who won a Silver at the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Games and bronze at the 2018 Jakarta-Palembang Games.Indian rowers Satnam Singh and Salman Khan won Bronze medal in the Men’s Double Sculls event this morning. The Indian pair stayed in second place until the 1,500m mark before slipping to third in the final 500m. China’s Yi Xudi and Yide Nie won the gold medal, while Uzbekistan’s Pavel Sorin and Mekhrojbek Mamatkulov claimed silver. Satnam had won a bronze at the Hangzhou Asian Games in the men’s quadruple sculls event.

. The Archaeological Survey of India has notified Gollala Gudi Temple at Palampet in the Mulugu district of Telangana as a monument of national importance. The Ministry of culture said that the temple is situated near the UNESCO listed Ramappa Temple and is renowned for its exquisite carvings and architectural heritage.The temple is a Trikutalaya and consists of a mandapa facing East and surrounded by three garbhagriha.A monument of national importance in the country is protected under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958. The Archaeological Survey of India takes charge of such sites for conservation, maintenance, and regulated public access

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will interact today via video conference with participants of Seva Yatra travelling from Vadnagar to Varanasi under Seva Sankalp Abhiyan.The interaction with the Prime Minister will give the Seva Yatris a chance to share their experiences from the journey, which is intended to connect youth participation and community service across the locations covered by the teams. The Seva Yatra began on September 17 and is part of the wider ‘Seva Sankalp Abhiyan’ to highlight PM Modi’s 25 years of public life. The participants are travelling through towns, districts, talukas and villages, with the programme focusing on taking community service and public engagement activities to the grassroots.The journey is not limited to a motorcycle expedition, but is designed to bring together service, communication, youth participation, social welfare, cultural connect and community mobilisation at different locations along the route. Ten groups are undertaking the Vadnagar-to-Varanasi journey. The two-way motorcycle yatras between Vadnagar and Varanasi involve young participants travelling across multiple states, districts and villages. During the journey, the Seva Yatris have engaged with local communities and participated in service-oriented activities.These include cleanliness drives and interactions with beneficiaries and residents, as well as activities at schools, hospitals, nursing homes, and other community locations. The journey is scheduled to continue until October 7. The broader campaign was launched from Vadnagar on September 17 by Union Home Minister Amit Shah and Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel, with the Vadnagar-to-Varanasi bike yatra being flagged off as part of the initiative. The wider motorcycle initiative includes journeys in both directions between Vadnagar, associated with PM Modi’s early life, and Varanasi, his Lok Sabha constituency.

. The US-Iran conflict has entered a new phase this week. While economic pressure on Iran is mounting, diplomatic contacts between the two have also resumed at UNGA in New York.In the UAE, the Central Bank (CBUAE) has imposed strict enforcement measures on the UAE branches of Bank Melli Iran. All UAE branches of the Iranian bank have been prohibited from conducting financial transactions to and from Iran, including trade finance and fund transfers. The action followed violations of UAE laws and regulatory requirements relating to money laundering, terrorism financing and proliferation financing. Bank Melli Iran is traditionally recognised as the oldest and largest state-owned commercial bank in Iran. Last month, the UAE decided to suspend all trade, commercial exchanges and financial transactions with Iran.Iran’s international air connectivity has also come under growing pressure. The United States has threatened secondary sanctions against companies that continue to provide Iranian airlines with services such as fuel, landing facilities and ticket sales. It has been reported that flights of Iranian Airlines toor fromvarious destinations were cancelled or suspended, includinginTurkey, Oman, Iraq, Georgia, and Azerbaijan.Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian addressed the UN General Assembly on Wednesday, saying Tehran would not surrender in its war with the United States while also expressing commitment to diplomacy. On the other hand, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that any agreement with Iran would require “a lot of hard work over a period of time” and the involvement of mediators. He also said that the US President had all the options, including “military”.  The US and Iran had held talks in New York on Tuesday through mediators including Qatar. The talks involved Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and US envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.In yet another incident in the Strait of Hormuz, an Indian national was killed when the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged commercial vessel MV Cape Dao was attacked off Oman’s coast. 19 other Indian seafarers aboard were rescued. Condemning the attacks on commercial shipping, India called for dialogue, diplomacy, and the restoration of free and unimpeded navigation through international waterways in the region.In Yemen, fighting has intensified around the Kahboub mountain range, which overlooks the strategic Bab El-Mandeb Strait. The Houthis are battling the pro-Government forces for control of the area. While the United States has so far stopped short of directly entering the latest Saudi-Houthi fighting, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio remarked that the US has a very strong defence agreement with Saudi Arabia and will live up to its commitments in that agreement. He also expressed happiness to see that “the Saudis were able to restart the pipeline again”. Media reports had earlier stated that Saudi Arabia had restarted the important East-West Pipeline which was shut following a drone attack.

. In Ladakh, RNU Akashvani Kargil has launched a special podcast series under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, with the first programme focusing on “Natural Farming – Towards Sustainable and Climate-Resilient Agriculture.”The programme featured Dr. Nazir Hussain, Scientist, Krishi Vigyan Kendra Kargil, in conversation with Anayat Ali of RNU Akashvani Kargil.During the podcast, Dr. Nazir Hussain explained the principles of natural farming and highlighted its role in improving soil health, reducing dependence on external chemical inputs and promoting sustainable and climate-resilient agriculture.He discussed various aspects of the National Mission on Natural Farming, including chemical-free cultivation, livestock integration, diversified cropping, use of locally available bio-inputs and integration of traditional agricultural knowledge with scientific practices.Dr. Hussain said natural farming has considerable potential in Ladakh and Kargil, where agriculture is characterised by a short growing season, cold climatic conditions and limited water availability. He stressed the need for locally adapted practices, scientific research, farmer training and awareness for its successful adoption in the region.Comparing natural farming with organic farming, Dr. Hussain said natural farming can be more effective and efficient in boosting production while reducing farmers’ dependence on externally purchased inputs.The discussion also covered crop productivity, input costs, farmers’ income, water management, climate resilience and the need to make the transition towards natural farming economically viable for farmers.The special podcast series, produced by RNU Akashvani Kargil under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, will be broadcast daily at 4:30 PM from Akashvani Kargil. The programmes will also be available on the AIRNews Kargil YouTube channel.

. The Government has announced the Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Awards for the year 2024. The awards recognise outstanding achievements by individuals in the field of adventure and seek to promote a spirit of endurance, risk-taking, teamwork and quick and effective decision-making in challenging situations. The awards are given in four categories, which are Land Adventure, Water Adventure, Air Adventure and Lifetime Achievement. Each awardee will receive a statuette, a certificate and award money of 15 lakh rupees. The awardees are Baljeet Kaur and Skalzang Rigzin in Land Adventure category, Rimo Saha in Water Adventure category and Shiv Prasad Chamoli in the Life Time Achievement category.The selections were made following the recommendations of the National Selection Committee. The Committee evaluated the nominations and recommended the awardees for conferment of the national honour.The awards seek to promote among the youth a spirit of courage, endurance, discipline, risk-taking and cooperative teamwork, while encouraging the ability to respond with speed and effectiveness in challenging situations. President Droupadi Murmu will confer the awards along with the National Sports Awards 2025. The date of the award ceremony will be announced later.

. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar met US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly session today.During the meeting, India and the US has discussed bilateral relations and New Delhi’s raised concerns regarding the sanctioning Russia and Iran Act.US President Donald Trump signed into law the “Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026” last week, which authorises him to impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on countries buying Russian oil and gas, including China and India.In its reaction, New Delhi said that it will take all necessary steps to protect its economic interests and ensure energy security for the nation.Jaishankar, who arrived in New York City on Sunday, is leading the Indian delegation for the 81st session of the UN General Assembly.After meeting with Jaishankar, Rubio said that India and the US are coordinating on key regional priorities. He added together, both countries are building strategic partnership and coordinating on key regional priorities and upcoming multilateral efforts.Earlier, two leaders also met in Manila in July this year and discussed priority areas including trade, tariffs, energy, defence, critical minerals, and artificial intelligence.

Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Bhupender Yadav today met Australia’s Minister for Climate Change and Energy and President of the COP31 negotiations Chris Bowen, in New Delhi.In a social media post, Mr Yadav informed that they discussed key agenda items for the upcoming Pre-COP in Fiji and COP31 in Turkey. He also highlighted the success stories of India’s ambitious climate action under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the past decade. Mr Yadav further reaffirmed India’s commitment to being a supportive partner to Australia in its role as President of the COP31 negotiations.

. Delhi Urban Development Minister Ashish Sood has announced the release of the second installment of the Basic Tax Assignment for the civic bodies of the National Capital. An amount of over Rs 1,850 crore has been sanctioned for the current financial year for the Municipal Corporation of Delhi, New Delhi Municipal Council and Delhi Cantonment Board.The funds will support essential municipal and civic services across the national capital, including waste collection and disposal, repair and maintenance of neighbourhood roads, streetlights and local parks. Mr Sood said the government is committed to transforming Delhi’s urban infrastructure and ensuring financial support for public welfare. He said timely release of funds is being ensured so that development works continue without any hurdles.

. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) today absorbed 75,026 crore rupees from the banking system through an overnight Variable Rate Reverse Repo (VRRR) auction, amid surplus liquidity. The RBI absorbed the liquidity at a cut-off and weighted average rate of 5.24 per cent.According to RBI data, as on 22nd September, liquidity in the banking system was in surplus of 4.45 trillion rupees. The RBI has been conducting VRRR auctions to absorb excess liquidity and align overnight money market rates with the repo rate. The central bank has also conducted open market operations (OMO) sales of government securities worth 50,000 crore rupees on 17th September and 25,000 crore rupees on 21st September.The remaining 25,000 crore rupees tranche is scheduled for 28th September. The RBI had announced total OMO sales of one trillion rupees in three tranches to manage liquidity conditions.

. External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar co-chaired the L.69 Consultative Ministerial Interaction on UNSC reform, along with his Saint Lucian counterpart Alva Baptist. Addressing the meeting, Dr Jaishankar noted that the Global South is at the receiving end of the unprecedented changes that the world is undergoing, with the UN falling short of expectations.The L.69 Consultative Ministerial Interaction is a high-level diplomatic meeting focused heavily on the comprehensive reform of the United Nations Security Council (UNSC). The L.69 Group is a major coalition of over 30 developing nations spanning Asia, Africa, Latin America, the Caribbean, and the Pacific, primarily Small Island Developing States.Mr Jaishankar also underlined the inability of the UN Security Council to address on-going conflicts and threats to international peace and security only highlight the urgency of reform. He stressed that continuing to delay reform perpetuates historical injustice. He said that the members of the L.69 and C.10 join forces to keep pushing for UNSC reform.The L.69 Group of Developing Countries is a cross-regional coalition of developing nations focused on achieving comprehensive and urgent reform of the United Nations Security Council. The C-10 (Committee of Ten) is an African Union coalition of ten African countries created to champion the Common African Position on the United Nations Security Council.

. India and New Zealand Free Trade Agreement will come into force from 20th of October this year. Addressing a press conference in New Delhi, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said that the Agreement provides duty-free access for 100 per cent of Indian exports to New Zealand. He said, the strategic partnerships reflects the shared ambition to deepen this cooperation and aspirational goal of doubling bilateral trade in goods and services to almost 35 thousand crore rupees in the next 4 to 5 years.This will open new opportunities for Indian exports including textiles and apparel, leather and footwear, engineering goods, pharmaceuticals, agriculture and processed food products. At the same time, New Zealand will gain enhanced and access to the Indian market for products including wood, wool, sheep meat, and raw leather hides. The Agreement also creates new opportunities in services, investment and professional, student and youth mobility, including enhanced pathways for Indian professionals and students.It provides for facilitating 20 billion US dollars of investment into India and strengthens bilateral cooperation in areas including agricultural productivity, pharmaceuticals and medical devices, traditional medicine and AYUSH, technology and trade facilitation. India and New Zealand share longstanding and close relations, anchored in strong people-to-people ties and expanding cooperation across trade and investment, agriculture, education, sports, technology and other areas. The FTA represents a significant step in further strengthening these ties and creating new opportunities for businesses and communities in both countries.

. Today is World Suicide Prevention Day. The day is observed worldwide to raise awareness about suicide prevention and the importance of mental health.The occasion reminds us that people facing emotional distress or difficult circumstances need timely support, understanding and appropriate care. Experts emphasise that listening to someone with patience and without judgement can encourage them to seek help and support.On this Day, people are encouraged to remain attentive to the emotional well-being of those around them and, when required, guide them towards family members, trusted persons or mental health professionals.

. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has proposed a single-phase rollout of Front-of-Pack Nutrition Labelling for packaged foods high in salt, sugar or fat. In an affidavit filed before the Supreme Court, the food regulator proposed a red hexagon warning label on the front of such products, specifying the nutrient exceeding the prescribed limit.FSSAI said the proposal will undergo public and industry consultations before finalisation. It has estimated that the draft regulations could be finalised within about four months after the consultation process.

. The Government today clarified that GST on UPI Merchant Discount Rate, or MDR, will not burden small merchants or make digital payments expensive. In a social media post, National Payments Corporation of India  (NPCI) has termed such media reports as incorrect. It said, MDR applies only to person-to-merchant transactions above two thousand rupees. It said person-to-merchant transactions up to two thousand rupees continue to have zero MDR and therefore zero GST impact. NPCI stated that transactions of up to two thousand rupees constitute more than 96 per cent of UPI merchant transaction volume. The GST paid on MDR by a merchant will be adjusted against the GST payable on the sale of goods, in the same manner that input taxes are set off against output tax liability. NPCI said that merchants with monthly UPI receipts of up to one lakh rupees are not liable to pay MDR.

. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar held a series of bilateral and multilateral meetings in New York on the sidelines of United Nations General Assembly, focusing on trade, investment, climate change, technology and geopolitical issues. Dr Jaishankar met his Netherlands counterpart Tom Berendsen and discussed the Ukraine conflict and followed up on commitments from Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to the Netherlands earlier this year.He also met Finland’s Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen and discussed geopolitical and technological challenges and bilateral cooperation with the European Union.In separate bilateral meetings, Dr Jaishankar held talks with Slovenia’s Foreign Minister Tomaž Kajzer on trade and investment opportunities linked to the proposed India-EU free trade agreement, along with energy, manufacturing, digital connectivity, defense and multilateral cooperation.At the India-CARICOM Foreign Ministers’ Meeting, Mr. Jaishankar stressed historical and developmental ties and highlighted India’s support for health care, quick-impact projects, training and renewable energy in the Caribbean. He called for deeper cooperation in economic, digital and mobility sectors.Mr. Jaishankar also highlighted India’s cooperation with Pacific island countries on climate resilience, space, sustainable coastal and ocean research. He said India was ready to help address the effects of El Niño and encouraged Pacific nations to join the International Solar Alliance and the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure.He also chaired the India-Pacific Islands Forum (FIPIC) Foreign Ministers’ Meeting, reaffirming India’s demand-driven, development-oriented and people-centric approach to the Pacific. He highlighted India’s support for the Pacific Islands Forum’s 2050 Strategy for the Blue Pacific Continent and outlined progress under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Action Plan covering health care, renewable energy, connectivity, technology and capacity building.With Andorra’s Foreign Minister Imma Tor Faus to discuss trade and investment, climate change, artificial intelligence and multilateral cooperation.

India’s men’s badminton team settled for the bronze medal after a 3-1 defeat to China in the semi-final in Aichi, Japan today.Indian player Lakshya Sen lost the opening match 21-16, 21-18 to Shi Yuqi before Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty levelled the tie with a 21-11, 22-20 win over reigning world champions Liang Wei Keng and Wang Chang.Ayush Shetty then lost 21-19, 21-13 to defending Asian Games champion Li Shifeng, while Hariharan Amsakarunan and MR Arjun went down fighting 21-16, 17-21, 21-9 to China’s He Ji Ting and Liu Yi in the fourth match.The bronze medal takes India’s overall tally to 12 medals – 1 gold, 5 silver and 6 bronze.

. Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh has said that critical minerals are key to India’s energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. The Minister said this while addressing a special plenary of the 3rd Global Summit on Advanced Materials, Critical Minerals, and Metals in New Delhi. Dr Singh said that critical minerals and metals will be a driving component of the next phase of technological development, with their importance extending beyond mining to energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. He said that the global economy is undergoing a paradigm shift, with clean energy, electric mobility, semiconductors, telecommunications, aerospace, defence and nuclear energy emerging as major drivers of technological and industrial transformation. He added, India is now participating in this global discourse with much greater confidence and is preparing to assume a larger global role.Dr. Singh has called for early industry linkage with research and innovation, saying potential industry partners should be brought on board right from the beginning. He further said that a healthy synergy among research, industry, government and the non-government sector is essential for sustaining startups and entrepreneurs. The Minister also highlighted on building domestic capabilities for energy security as the world moves towards cleaner and greener sources of energy. He said that India’s next phase of growth in strategic technologies and materials will depend on working together of all stakeholders.

. President Droupadi Murmu has congratulated Parinaaz Dhaliwal, Raiza Dhillon and Maheshwari Chauhan on winning the Bronze Medal in the Women’s Skeet Team event at the Asian Games. President Murmu also extended wishes to Anantjeet Singh Naruka, Bhavtegh Singh Gill and Mairaj Ahmad Khan on securing a Bronze Medal in the Men’s Skeet Team.In a social media post, the President said that their skill, determination and team spirit have made the nation proud. President Murmu also extended her best wishes to them for achieving even greater success in the future.Prime Minister Narendra Modi today congratulated Parinaaz Dhaliwal, Maheshwari Chauhan, and Raiza Dhillon on winning the Bronze Medal in the Women’s Skeet Team event at the Asian Games held in Japan. In a social media post, Mr Modi said that their focus, precision and teamwork have brought another proud moment for Indian sports. He further extended his best wishes to them for their upcoming endeavours.Prime Minister Narendra Modi also congratulated Mirabai Chanu on winning a Silver medal in the Women’s 49 kilogram Weightlifting event. In a social media post, the Prime Minister stated that her determination and consistency continue to inspire the nation. He further extended his best wishes for Mirabai Chanu’s future endeavours.Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr Mansukh Mandaviya congratulated Parinaaz Dhaliwal, Raiza Dhillon and Maheshwari Chauhan on securing the first-ever Bronze Medal in the Women’s Skeet Team event at the Asian Games.Mr Mandaviya extended wishes to Anantjeet Singh Naruka, Bhavtegh Singh Gill and Mairaj Ahmad Khan on securing the Bronze Medal in the Men’s Skeet Team.He also congratulated Mirabai Chanu on winning the Silver Medal in the Women’s 49kg Weightlifting event at the Asian Games and described it as a proud moment for the nation. In a social media post, Mr Mandaviya said this is Ms Chanu’s first Asian Games medal and stated that this brings India another medal at the Games after 28 years.He also congratulated Jay Meena on securing the first-ever Bronze Medal in the Men’s Singles Soft Tennis event at the Asian Games.

. India has extended anti-dumping duty on decor papers imported from China till March next year to protect domestic manufacturers from cheap inbound shipments. In December 2021, the Department of Revenue imposed the duty in the range of USD 110 per tonne to USD 542 per tonne, for five years. The department has amended a notification to extend the levy of anti-dumping duty on imports of ‘Decor Paper’ originating in or exported from People’s Republic of China, up to and inclusive of 26th March, 2027.

. At the Asian Games, the Indian trio of Maheshwari Singh, Parinaaz Dhaliwal and Raiza Dhillon secured the bronze medal in the women’s team skeet shooting event at Aichi-Nagoya, taking country’s overall medal tally on Day 4 to eight.In another feat, Jay Meena made history in soft tennis, assuring country its first-ever medal in the sport. Jay has advanced to the semifinals, defeating Sherwin Nuguit of the Philippines 4-3 in a closely fought quarterfinal.In shooting, Double Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker has qualified for the final of women’s 10-metre air pistol event. However, the trio of Manu, Suruchi Singh and Esha Singh failed to qualify in the team event.Indian swimmer Beniston Benedicton has qualified for the final of the men’s 100-metre butterfly event. He finished ninth overall in the heats to secure his place in the final which will be held at 1:38 PM today.In rowing at the Asian Games, Balraj Panwar has qualified for the final of the men’s singles sculls event. He finished third in his heat with a timing of 6 minutes 52.84 seconds and was fourth overall across the two heats. The final will be held tomorrow. India have also secured final berth in the men’s double sculls event. Satnam Singh and Salman Khan finished second in their heat, clocking 6 minutes 15.63 seconds. The match is scheduled to begin at 10 AM. In Wushu, Roshibina Devi will face Indonesia’s Thania Kusumaningtyas in the women’s 60-kilogram Sanda semi-final at 2:50 PM.India’s skeet shooters Anantjeet Singh Naruka, Bhavtegh Singh Gill and Mairaj Ahmad Khan will be in action on the final day of qualification.In Hockey, the Indian Women’s Team will face Thailand in their third Pool B match this morning.
